description: T-4164: what Excel for the web keeps for a Top-N filter at its edges. Data!A1:B7 has Product and Sales in source order Kiwi 30, Apple 50, Fig 30, Date 20, Pear 10, Lime 10 (total 150): two ties at 30 (cache order Kiwi then Fig, alphabetical Fig then Kiwi) and two at 10 (cache Pear then Lime). Each sheet is one builder-v2 pivot at A3, rows Product, Sum of Sales, with one `<filter fld="0" iMeasureFld="0">` whose top10 filterVal equals its val: TC2 count top 2 (tie at the cut-off); TB1 count bottom 1 (tie); TC9 count top 9 of 6 items; TP40 percent top 40 (threshold 60 reached on a tied item); TPb5 percent bottom 5 (threshold 7.5, reached on a tied item); TS50 sum top 50 (reached exactly by Apple); TS60 sum top 60 (reached on a tied item, the threshold of TP40); TS110 sum top 110 (reached exactly by Apple, Kiwi and Fig); TSb10 sum bottom 10 (reached exactly by either tied 10). Which tied item a percent or sum filter takes: TP40i and TSb10i are TP40 and TSb10 with the field's `<item>` elements listing Fig (Lime) first (`item_order`; the cache and the source keep Kiwi and Pear first); TP40o and TSb10o write the cache, and the items with it, with Fig (Lime) first (`order`; the source still has Kiwi and Pear first). Neg!A1:B6 has Item and Amt A 1, B 0, C -3, D -8, E 2 (total -8); rows Item, Sum of Amt: NT3 count top 3 (a zero at the cut-off); NB2 count bottom 2; NP50 percent top 50 of a negative total; NBP50 percent bottom 50; NS3 sum top 3 (reached exactly by E and A, a zero next); NBS sum bottom 10 (a negative val, top or bottom, makes the web refuse the file: pivots.md). Pivot cells are in the sidecar's `pivots` section; Q!A1 makes the case scored.
